prohibited_recommendations: Do not proceed to a shunt evaluation on the strength of the clinical triad alone when the imaging shows ex vacuo ventriculomegaly and a severe small-vessel burden
Do not add anticoagulation: there is no cardioembolic indication and four deep microbleeds raise haemorrhagic risk
Do not prescribe anticholinergic bladder agents for the urinary urgency
Do not drop blood pressure precipitously in severe small-vessel disease; titrate with renal monitoring
Do not attribute the falls to age or to arthritis without measuring gait
required_recommendations: Document the cognitive deficit with education-adjusted instruments
Exclude reversible causes with the named screen and interpret them alongside the renal impairment
Obtain brain MRI with SWI and grade the burden in STRIVE-2 terms
Measure gait objectively and act on a timed-up-and-go of 24.6 s as a falls emergency
Distinguish this syndrome from normal pressure hydrocephalus on the ventricular measurements and the gait pattern before considering a tap test
Lower blood pressure toward target while monitoring renal function
Address home safety, medication supervision and caregiver support

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

accepted: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type, severe hypertensive arteriopathy with gait failure

differential.key_features: Gait failure with urinary urgency and cognitive impairment is the NPH triad, but the Evans index is 0.30 with ventriculomegaly proportionate to atrophy, there is no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space, and the gait is short-stepped rather than magnetic; the Fazekas 3 burden with eight lacunes explains the syndrome without invoking hydrocephalus
Cue-responsive recall, preserved medial temporal lobes and gait failure early in the course are all against it

Lower-body predominant gait disorder from the same small-vessel burden is a reasonable label for the motor syndrome, but there is no rest tremor, no rigidity and no levodopa responsiveness to establish
Stage 3b disease is a genuine contributor and shares the same hypertensive cause, but does not account for eight lacunes and a Fazekas 3 burden
No fluctuation, hallucinations, parkinsonism or dream enactment

key_clinical_evidence: The NPH triad and severe small-vessel disease overlap almost completely in their clinical presentation; the discrimination is made on ventricular morphology, the disproportion of the subarachnoid spaces and the character of the gait, not on the triad itself
Hypertensive end-organ damage in the kidney, heart and retina corroborates the vascular attribution in a patient with no dateable stroke
A strictly deep microbleed distribution indicates hypertensive arteriopathy and, unlike a lobar distribution, does not by itself prohibit antithrombotic therapy
A timed-up-and-go of 24.6 s is a falls emergency and is actionable immediately, whereas no further imaging changes management
Education-adjusted norms are necessary to avoid overcalling impairment in a patient with ten years of schooling — and here the deficit survives the adjustment

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Urinary urgency in severe small-vessel disease is part of the frontal-subcortical syndrome; prostatism coexists, and neither observation supports hydrocephalus in the absence of the imaging phenotype
red_herrings.data_point: Urinary urgency with known prostatic hyperplasia
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attributes the urinary symptom to the prostate and removes it from the neurological syndrome, or conversely completes an NPH triad

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: An Evans index of 0.30 with ventriculomegaly proportionate to parenchymal loss, no disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid space, and a Fazekas 3 burden with eight lacunes is ex vacuo dilatation in severe small-vessel disease
red_herrings.data_point: Ventricular enlargement with the full clinical triad
red_herrings.intended_effect: Leads to a diagnosis of normal pressure hydrocephalus and to a tap test or shunt referral

social_history.living_situation: Lives with his son's family; his daughter-in-law manages his medication

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Samuel Adeyemi is a 78-year-old retired bus driver who lives with his son and attends with his daughter-in-law. Over two years he has become progressively slower in thought and in movement, and over the past year he has fallen three times, always while turning or rising. The family's chief concern is safety: he leaves the tap running, cannot manage his own medication, and last month took a bus in the wrong direction and had to be collected. His memory for recent events is patchy but improves markedly when he is reminded of the setting; his daughter-in-law says he 'knows it when you tell him where it happened'. He has no discrete episodes of weakness or speech loss that the family can date. He has had hypertension for thirty-five years, was lost to follow-up for a long period in his fifties, and now has stage 3b chronic kidney disease and left ventricular hypertrophy attributed to it. His blood pressure at this visit is 176/96 despite three agents. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation across the day, no dream enactment and no rest tremor. Urinary urgency is present and has been attributed to his prostate.

neurological_exam.additional: Frontal release signs present. Urinary frequency and urgency, partly attributed to prostatism. No tremor, no rigidity.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact in the upper limbs; mild bilateral heel-to-shin clumsiness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundi show grade 2 hypertensive retinopathy with arteriolar narrowing and arteriovenous nipping. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech mildly dysarthric.
neurological_exam.gait: Markedly short-stepped, wide-based, low clearance, with preserved arm swing. Requires the chair arms to rise. Turns in six steps. Three falls in the past year. Tandem impossible.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, year correct, date incorrect by four days. MoCA 21/30 with losses in trail-making, clock, digit span backwards, fluency (10 animals) and delayed recall (3/5 unaided, 5/5 cued). Answers are correct but slow.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Tone increased in both legs. Strength 5/5 with 4+/5 hip flexion bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ knees, 2+ ankles, plantar responses extensor bilaterally. Palmomental present.
